label: Oil Production
change: Chevron and PDVSA signed an updated joint-venture agreement Sept 2 covering additional Orinoco Belt acreage and $7B+ in investment over five years, targeting a doubling of Chevron JV output to ~600K bpd (costs held below $20/barrel); Eni separately expanded its Venezuelan oil projects the same week; Hydrocarbons Minister Paula Henao and PDVSA's Jovanny Martínez told a Houston investor showcase on Aug 19 that national output stands at ~1.25M bpd, with a long-term recovery target of 3M bpd, aided by the January regulatory reform expanding private participation across the value chain
source: World Oil / Bloomberg / EIA / Chevron / PDVSA (Sep 2, 2026)

label: Annual Inflation
change: Monthly inflation slowed sharply to an 18-month low of 8.9% in August (from 19.9% in July), which the BCV attributed to lower currency-market pressure and a smaller move in the exchange rate; prices are still up 534.2% year-on-year and ~200% since January; the official bolívar rate broke past 800/USD for the first time in August (804.81 on Sep 3) and reached 857.01/USD by Sep 25 — roughly a fivefold depreciation over 12 months; IMF projects ~682% inflation for full-year 2026

label: GDP (USD)
change: IMF April 2026 WEO projects +4.0% real GDP growth for 2026; oil sector recovery and post-Maduro international re-engagement driving rebound; IMF and World Bank resumed formal engagement post-transition

label: PDVSA Oil Revenue
change: −85% from ~$80B peak; oil investment +55% to $1.4B in 2026

label: Potential Banking Liquidity Injection
change: OFAC General Licenses expanded under political transition

label: Earthquake Damage & Reconstruction Cost
change: World Bank's August 2026 assessment placed physical damage at ~$19.6–20B, versus the UN's earlier $37B estimate including reconstruction; World Bank warned 'build back better' costs could reach $50B and GDP may stay below pre-earthquake levels until 2036 without sufficient investment; Rodríguez government secured $346M in emergency IMF financing plus $300M pledged by the US and $36.5M from the European Commission, but the UN's $931M 2026 humanitarian appeal remained only 39% funded as of early August
